notes.headline: Workday lifts its margin and subscription outlook as AI products bring in nearly $150 million of new contract value
notes.takeaway: Subscription revenue rose 12.8% to $2.53 billion and the adjusted operating margin widened to 31.4%. AI products added nearly $150 million in new annual contract value, more than triple a year ago. Workday raised its full-year subscription guide to $9.958 billion and its margin target to 31.5%.
results: Total revenue was $2.705 billion, up 11.2%, and subscription revenue $2.532 billion, up 12.8%. The 12-month subscription backlog grew 12.3% to $9.216 billion, while the total backlog grew 6.1% to $27.548 billion.

GAAP operating income was $329 million, a 12.1% margin, after $51 million of restructuring costs; the adjusted operating margin rose to 31.4% from 28.5%. Adjusted EPS was $2.82 against $2.32 a year earlier. Free cash flow was $691 million, and Workday bought back 3.8 million shares for $750 million, ending with $5.64 billion in cash and securities.
mgmt: Co-founder and chief executive Aneel Bhusri said AI products drove nearly $150 million in new annual contract value, more than three times last year, and that the focus now is moving more agents into production so customers see the value sooner. More than 2,200 core customers have bought at least one AI product.

Chief financial officer Zane Rowe raised the full-year subscription revenue forecast to $9.958 billion, 13% growth, and the adjusted operating margin to 31.5%. For the fourth quarter Workday guides to subscription revenue of $2.600 billion, up 10%, with a 31.7% margin.
view: The quarter answers one of the main worries around Workday: that AI agents would shrink the number of paid seats in HR software. So far the opposite is happening. AI products are being bought on top of the core suite, and the growth in the 12-month backlog matches subscription growth, which means current demand is holding up.

The weaker spot is the outlook. Fourth-quarter subscription growth of 10% would be a clear slowdown from 12.8%, and total backlog growing only 6% says fewer long multi-year deals are being signed than before. Workday is becoming a steady low-teens grower whose earnings rise faster than revenue thanks to cost cuts and buybacks. The shares rose only 0.7% to $180.44.

At around 14 to 15 times forward earnings, the market is paying for that slower profile and not much more. If AI contract value keeps tripling it becomes material within two years and growth could re-accelerate; if not, the stock is a margin-and-buyback story whose return depends on the size of repurchases. Both outcomes look reasonably priced from here.
notes.watch: Whether fourth-quarter subscription growth lands near 10% or better, the share of new contract value coming from AI products, and the first guidance for fiscal 2028 in late February.
